author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose distorted or clipped PS2 audio
summary: Compare loud and quiet passages at safe volume, correlate artifacts with speed and route, bypass processing, and change buffering only when evidence indicates underruns.
heroAlt: Phantom game scene used to compare quiet ambience and loud effects while checking PS2 audio distortion

blocks.text: Classify distortion by level, workload, and route

Record one quiet passage, one loud passage, and one CPU-heavy scene at moderate fixed volume. Bypass Android equalizers, spatial effects, and hearing enhancements, and confirm the game runs at full speed. Capture emulator speed and audio-buffer behavior alongside a direct recording so peak clipping can be separated from crackle that appears when the buffer starves.

Maximum phone volume can overload the speaker or adapter even when the emulator signal is clean. Do not diagnose by loudness alone, and do not change latency, synchronization, volume, and renderer in one attempt. Preserve an unaffected quiet sample; it is the reference that reveals whether distortion follows signal level or workload.
Capture one quiet and one loud reference

items: Phone volume reduced from maximum to a safe repeatable level.
Emulation-speed indicator available for correlation.
Android enhancements and output route recorded.
Save level-matched recordings of a quiet passage, a loud transient, and a CPU-heavy scene with Android audio effects bypassed.
Align the waveform with emulation-speed and buffer evidence to see whether damage follows signal peaks, workload spikes, or one output route.

blocks.text: Change gain, workload, and route independently

items: 1. Play the quiet passage and record hiss, crackle, or tonal distortion.
2. Play the loud passage at the same moderate system volume.
3. Lower volume one controlled step and note whether only peak distortion changes.
4. Watch emulation speed when clicks or gaps occur.
5. Disable one Android effect for a paired comparison.
6. Move to phone speakers or a known wired output without changing emulator timing.
7. Test a second game and ordinary media through the same device.
8. Adjust audio buffering only if artifacts correlate with underruns rather than amplitude.

blocks.text: Clipping repeats on the same loud peaks and often shows flattened waveform tops. Underrun crackle follows frame-time spikes or speed drops, while time-stretch artifacts follow correction activity. If non-emulator music distorts through the same route, bypass the speaker, DAC, Bluetooth codec, or Android effect before altering EmuCoreX.

Speech, music, and sharp transients must remain clean through a sustained full-speed run at the matched level. Repeat the loud passage after reconnecting the output route and replay the CPU-heavy scene after shader compilation has settled. Save recordings that include the first failure and the corrected pass.

items: Loud effects do not flatten or buzz at the accepted level.
Quiet passages remain continuous without workload-linked gaps.
The result survives a route reconnect and a sustained scene.
The corrected capture must preserve clean loud peaks and quiet detail while a second game and ordinary media remain unchanged at that level.
Cold-launch the title, warm the heavy scene, reconnect the output, and reproduce both reference passages without touching synchronization settings.
Artifact vanishes with lower volume in all apps: avoid output-stage clipping.
Clicks coincide with speed drops: solve performance before audio cosmetics.
One headset distorts ordinary media: replace or reconfigure that route.
One recorded line in one game is distorted: verify source behavior before global tuning.

blocks.text: Restore audio gain and timing baseline

Return buffer, synchronization, volume, and Android effects to the recorded baseline in reverse order. Keep only the single setting whose effect was repeatable, then verify a second game and ordinary media. If distortion belongs to one source asset or title, remove the global experiment rather than dulling audio across the library.

Two faults can coexist: a workload spike may underrun while a loud Bluetooth or speaker path clips. Use separate level-matched and load-matched comparisons, and report which passage triggers each artifact. A clean waveform captured before the physical output helps distinguish emulator signal quality from downstream amplification.
